title: Indian-Origin NASA Astronaut Anil Menon Arrives at the International Space Station on First Mission
excerpt: The son of Indian and Ukrainian immigrants becomes the first American to reach space since the Artemis II moon mission, launching from Kazakhstan aboard a Russian Soyuz spacecraft.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Anil Menon, 49, is the first American in space since April 2026.
  • He launched aboard Soyuz MS-29 from Kazakhstan on July 14.
  • Menon will spend eight months conducting research on the ISS.
  • His wife, Anna Menon, is also a NASA astronaut.
  • Menon's mission highlights the Indian diaspora's growing presence in space.
Anil Menon's Journey to Space
July 14, 2026
Launch aboard Soyuz MS-29 from Baikonur Cosmodrome, Kazakhstan.
July 15, 2026
Arrived at the International Space Station after a three-hour journey.
April 2027
Scheduled return to Earth after eight months on the ISS.
  • NASA astronaut Anil Menon, 49, arrived at the International Space Station on July 15 aboard a Soyuz MS-29 spacecraft after a three-hour journey from Kazakhstan
  • Menon is the son of Indian and Ukrainian immigrants, born in Minneapolis, and is an emergency medicine physician and U.S. Space Force colonel
  • He is the first American to reach space since the landmark Artemis II moon mission ended in April 2026
  • His wife, Anna Menon, is also a NASA astronaut who flew to space on the private Polaris Dawn mission in 2024

NASA astronaut Anil Menon and two Russian cosmonauts arrived safely at the International Space Station on July 15, completing a three-hour orbital journey from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan. The mission marks Menon's first spaceflight and makes him the first American to reach orbit since the Artemis II crew returned from their historic moon voyage in April.

Menon, 49, launched aboard the Soyuz MS-29 spacecraft alongside Roscosmos cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov and Anna Kikina at 10:47 a.m. EDT on July 14. The spacecraft docked with the station's Prichal module roughly three hours later, and the crew was welcomed aboard by the existing team of seven.

From Everest to Orbit

Born in Minneapolis to Indian and Ukrainian immigrants, Menon has built a career that spans military medicine, space operations, and commercial spaceflight. He served on the frontlines in Afghanistan during Operation Enduring Freedom as a U.S. Air Force physician and worked with the Himalayan Rescue Association caring for climbers on Mount Everest.

Menon spent a year in India as a Rotary Ambassadorial Scholar, supporting polio vaccination initiatives — a formative experience that deepened his connection to the subcontinent.

He joined NASA as a flight surgeon in 2014, then moved to SpaceX in 2018, where he helped establish the company's medical program and worked on Starship development. NASA selected him as an astronaut candidate in December 2021.

Menon's Research Focus on ISS
›Refining in-space production of semiconductor crystals for computing.
›Testing AI-assisted ultrasound techniques for deep-space missions.
›Studying microgravity effects on blood flow and vein structure.
›Conducting experiments over an eight-month stay aboard the ISS.

A Space Family

In a remarkable coincidence, Menon's wife, Anna Wilhelm Menon, is also an astronaut. She flew to space in September 2024 as part of the Polaris Dawn mission — a private SpaceX venture funded and commanded by Jared Isaacman, who is now NASA's administrator. Isaacman traveled to Baikonur for the Soyuz MS-29 launch, marking the first visit by a NASA chief to Russia's launch facility since 2018.

Eight Months of Research

During his approximately eight-month stay aboard the ISS as part of Expedition 75, Menon will conduct a range of experiments. His research portfolio includes refining in-space production of semiconductor crystals for high-performance computing and AI, testing augmented reality and AI-assisted ultrasound techniques that could eliminate the need for medical support from Earth on future deep-space missions, and studying how microgravity affects blood flow and vein structure in astronauts.

Menon is scheduled to return to Earth in April 2027.

What It Means

For the Indian diaspora, Menon's mission represents another milestone in the community's growing presence in space exploration. His appointment follows in the tradition of Kalpana Chawla and Sunita Williams, while his dual Indian-Ukrainian heritage underscores the diverse backgrounds of those pushing the boundaries of human spaceflight.
